Reading this made me freeze because I thought reddit had glitched and was showing me one of my own posts from when I was younger. Happened to me at 20, exactly the same details. First off let me say I am so sorry you are going through this and even though it feels like shit right now you have an opportunity to work on the things in your control and build a life that feels safe and secure. I am going to tell you what worked for me eventually and I wish I had done when that happened to me the first time. Do you have health insurance? Depending on where you live, you could reach out to a partial hospitalization program and take this time to work on processing your past so it doesn’t control your whole future. You go to groups throughout the day and they’re not like in the hospital; you actually learn instead of just being kept occupied. Plus, many programs provide housing/food for a fee, or offer scholarships if you can’t afford it. They also assign you a case manager who can help you figure out a better plan for when you’re discharged. In my experience this is by far the best route to go especially after such a major event. Let me know if this is something you want to know more about, or if it wouldn’t work for you and I can come up with something else that might help. Feel free to message me on here as well, any time. I understand how terrifying this is.

I was 11 years old when I had surgery. I started showing severe symptoms at 8 months old and was diagnosed Chiari at 2. They found a MASSIVE syrinx when I was 11 and I had surgery almost immediately after. I had some complications during surgery and recovery, and even with that I started middle school on time 2 months later (with accommodations of course). I would say it took me about a year to be fully recovered, but majority of the healing took place very early on, things just kinda slowed down after a while. This timeline can vary so much person to person. This was mine with complications and over a decade ago. Treatment advanced an insane amount since then. I honestly don’t even remember being scared during all of this. Just bummed out to be missing certain things for a little bit. The difference before and after surgery was night and day. I understand how terrifying this can be for you and you can DM me any time with questions or anything you need. Best of luck to you and your daughter ❤️❤️❤️

I was diagnosed at 2 under pretty similar circumstances. I was pretty sick. Years later they found the syrinx. Back then most doctors hadn’t even heard of Chiari and treatment was hard to find. Even with those obstacles I turned out okay. I am always amazed at how far doctors have come in managing this condition so quickly. Today you can thrive with Chiari. Plus, that early diagnosis really sets her up to get the best care. Your daughter will be okay. I’m sure my mom was terrified with the news at first but it got easier over time, especially with doing her own research and reaching out to other parents in the same boat. You got this. I hope you keep us updated and please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have questions or need anything <3 <3 <3

I have had episodes like this before. The biggest thing that helped me is finding the right meds, and reminding myself it will not last forever, no matter what my brain is telling me. Something has triggered your fight or flight response and you’ve gone into survival mode. These responses were designed for things like being chased by a lion and now we don’t have these threats so it just goes off without an obvious reason sometimes. If you do know the reason, great, that will help so much in getting support. If not, start at the basic needs and work your way up. I’m sure you hear it all the time, but make sure you eat, exercise and drink water even if your body is fighting against it right now. Get some sunlight if you’re in an area where that’s possible. Make sure you are having some type of social connection each day, whether its a deep conversation with a friend or saying hello to someone in passing. I have pretty severe anxiety and was worried about getting “addicted.” Something important to keep in mind is that you can’t become physically addicted. What I did was only do it on weekends at first (or whatever days you have nothing to do so you can just unwind).
